segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
And today we're talking about a very important day in a couple's life.
segments.zh: 今天我们谈论的是一对夫妇生活中非常重要的一天。

segments.en: But this time, it's not going to be so romantic because actually the groom is having second thoughts about the wedding.
segments.zh: 但这一次，它不会那么浪漫，因为实际上新郎正在对婚礼进行重新考虑。

segments.en: Okay, that means he's nervous and he's not positive he wants to get married today.
segments.zh: 好吧，这意味着他很紧张，他不肯定他今天想结婚。

segments.en: So remember the groom is the man, the bride is the woman.
segments.zh: 所以记住新郎是男人，新娘是女人。

segments.en: Let's jump right into this dialogue.
segments.zh: 让我们直接进入这个对话。

segments.en: Listen to what's going on and when we come back, we'll be talking about some of the words and phrases you've heard.
segments.zh: 听听正在发生的事情，当我们回来时，我们将谈论您听到的一些单词和短语。

segments.en: Jeez, you're sweating like a pig.
I can't go through with this.
I've got my entire life ahead of me.
segments.zh: 我的一生都在等待着我。

segments.en: It wasn't more than a month ago that you were rambling on about how you are tired of living the life of a bachelor and how you envy your friends that have a family.
segments.zh: 不到一个月前，你还一直念叨，说受够了单身生活，多么羡慕那些成家了的朋友。

segments.en: First of all, you cannot leave Amy at the altar.
segments.zh: 首先，你不能在婚礼上抛下艾米。

segments.en: Not only will she be humiliated and kill you, but she is the woman that you love and the woman of your dreams.
segments.zh: 那不仅会让她受辱，气得想杀了你，而且她是你深爱的人，是你的梦中情人。

segments.en: Why would you want to end that or jeopardize it like this?
segments.zh: 你为什么要结束它或像这样危及它？

segments.en: Second of all, you are just getting cold feet.
segments.zh: 其次，你只是临阵退缩了。

segments.en: You know deep down inside that you want to marry her.
segments.zh: 你心里很清楚，你想娶她。

segments.en: So cut the crap and do it.
segments.zh: 所以别废话了，去结婚吧。

segments.en: Phew, that was a close one.
You had me going there for a minute.
segments.zh: 刚才有一阵我还真被你唬住了。

segments.en: I thought I was going to have to slap some sense into you.
segments.zh: 我还以为得抽你几巴掌才能让你清醒呢。

segments.en: So almost, he almost didn't get married, but luckily you have a good friend to help you out.
segments.zh: 所以几乎，他几乎没有结婚，但幸运的是你有一个好朋友可以帮助你。

segments.en: So this friend really saved the day, made sure that the groom didn't get too nervous and had some really positive words.
segments.zh: 所以这位朋友真的挽救了这一天，确保新郎不会太紧张，并且有一些非常积极的话。

segments.en: So let's take a listen to some of these marriage words in today's Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以让我们来听听今天的语言外卖中的一些婚姻词语。

segments.en: Alright, so as you mentioned, we have this word marriage.
segments.zh: 好吧，正如你提到的，我们有这个词婚姻。

segments.en: Now marriage is the noun form, right, of actually getting married or to be married.
segments.zh: 现在，婚姻是实际结婚或结婚的名词形式，对。

segments.en: Marriage is the noun, the word that describes the relationship between two married people.
segments.zh: 婚姻是名词，是描述两个已婚人之间关系的词。

segments.en: Okay, and so you have a relationship, maybe you're dating, but once you get married, the thing between you as a man and a woman, that's your marriage.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以你有一段关系，也许你正在约会，但一旦你结婚，你作为男人和女人之间的事情，这就是你的婚姻。

segments.en: You could say our marriage is in danger.
segments.zh: 你可以说我们的婚姻处于危险之中。

segments.en: We need to work on our marriage.
segments.zh: 我们需要为我们的婚姻而努力。

segments.en: Now if you get married, and this guy, he mentioned a phrase which was to settle down.
segments.zh: 现在，如果你和这个人结婚，他提到了一个要安定下来的短语。

segments.en: This is a very important phrase.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常重要的短语。

segments.en: To settle down means to get serious, mature, and to stop living like a child.
segments.zh: 安定下来意味着要认真、成熟，不再像孩子一样生活。

segments.en: It means really to have a house or to start having kids.
segments.zh: 这意味着真的有房子或开始生孩子。

segments.en: So to settle down is to become more stable, right?
segments.zh: 所以安定下来就是变得更加稳定，对吧？

segments.en: As you say, to buy a house, to have a family, to stay in one place and not be so adventurous or stuff like that.
segments.zh: 正如你所说，买房子，有家人，呆在一个地方，不要那么冒险或类似的东西。

segments.en: So it's to calm down and to be more fixed in life.
segments.zh: 所以它是为了冷静下来，在生活中更加固定。

segments.en: Now the opposite of this would be to be a bachelor.
segments.zh: 现在相反的是成为单身汉。

segments.en: So bachelor is a single man, someone who's not married.
segments.zh: 所以单身汉是单身男人，没有结婚的人。

segments.en: And you often hear this term when we talk about apartments.
segments.zh: 当我们谈论公寓时，你经常听到这个词。

segments.en: So bachelor pad is an apartment that's specific to a single man.
segments.zh: 所以单身汉是一个专门针对单身男人的公寓。

segments.en: Usually there's lots of video games and a fancy TV and a pool table.
segments.zh: 通常有很多电子游戏、一台花哨的电视和一张台球桌。

segments.en: We had a lesson about this called bachelor party.
segments.zh: 我们有一个关于这个叫做单身派对的课程。

segments.en: Which is a party for a man right before he gets married.
segments.zh: 这是一个男人结婚前的聚会。

segments.en: And bachelor is a special word for a man who's not yet married.
segments.zh: 对于尚未结婚的男人来说，单身汉是一个特殊的词。

segments.en: And now as they were talking about not getting married, he said that you can't leave Amy at the altar.
segments.zh: 而现在当他们谈论不结婚时，他说你不能把艾米留在祭坛上。

segments.en: So you often hear this in movies.
segments.zh: 所以你经常在电影中听到这一点。

segments.en: She got left at the altar or you can't leave her at the altar.
segments.zh: 她被留在祭坛上，或者你不能把她留在祭坛上。

segments.en: This word altar is actually religious.
segments.zh: 这个字祭坛实际上是宗教的。

segments.en: Altar is the table in a church where the priest does all of his work.
segments.zh: 祭坛是牧师在教堂里做他所有工作的桌子。

segments.en: So an altar is a special religious table.
segments.zh: 所以祭坛是一个特殊的宗教桌子。

segments.en: So usually two people will stand in front of an altar and get married right with the priest who is doing his thing there.
segments.zh: 所以通常两个人会站在祭坛前，与在那里做事的牧师结婚。

segments.en: He says, do you Joe take Samantha to be your bride?
segments.zh: 他说，乔你把萨曼莎当你的新娘了吗？

segments.en: So that happens at a special place called the altar.
segments.zh: 所以这发生在一个叫做祭坛的特殊地方。

segments.en: And not at the normal mass like on Sundays.
segments.zh: 而不是像周日那样的正常弥撒。

segments.en: And for the last word or phrase today, it's to get cold feet.
segments.zh: 对于今天的最后一个词或短语，它是为了冷静下来。

segments.en: So this is a very funny phrase in English because it doesn't actually mean that your cold feet are cold.
segments.zh: 所以这在英语中是一个非常有趣的短语，因为它实际上并不意味着你的冷脚是冷的。

segments.en: So cold feet means you're nervous about something.
segments.zh: 所以冷脚意味着你对某事感到紧张。

segments.en: So people often talk about men and women getting cold feet before a wedding.
segments.zh: 所以人们经常在婚礼前谈论男人和女人冷脚。

segments.en: But you can also relate it to any other situation, not only getting married.
segments.zh: 但您也可以将其与任何其他情况联系起来，而不仅仅是结婚。

segments.en: For example, I'm going to go jump out of an airplane tomorrow.
segments.zh: 例如，我明天要从飞机上跳下来。

segments.en: Oh no, I have cold feet.
I don't think I want to jump out of an airplane.
segments.zh: 我不认为我想跳下飞机。

segments.en: So that's to get cold feet.
To have second thoughts or doubts about actually doing something.
segments.zh: 对实际做某事有第二个想法或怀疑。

segments.en: So why don't we listen to our dialogue again.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不再听我们的对话。

segments.en: Let's keep a lookout for all of these words and we'll be back in a little bit.
segments.zh: 让我们留意所有这些词，我们会稍微回来。

segments.en: Jeez, you're sweating like a pig.
I can't go through with this.
I've got my entire life ahead of me.
segments.zh: 我的一生都在等待着我。

segments.en: It wasn't more than a month ago that you were rambling on about how you are tired of living the life of a bachelor and how you envy your friends that have a family.
segments.zh: 不到一个月前，你还一直念叨，说受够了单身生活，多么羡慕那些成家了的朋友。

segments.zh: 首先，你不能在婚礼上抛下艾米。

segments.zh: 你为什么要结束它或像这样危及它？

segments.zh: 其次，你只是临阵退缩了。

segments.en: You know deep down inside that you'd want to marry her.
segments.zh: 你内心深处知道你会想嫁给她。

segments.zh: 所以别废话了，去结婚吧。

segments.zh: 刚才有一阵我还真被你唬住了。

segments.zh: 我还以为得抽你几巴掌才能让你清醒呢。

segments.en: So now why don't we take a look at four key phrases that we found in this dialogue on Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 那么现在我们为什么不看看我们在 Fluency Builder 的对话中找到的四个关键短语。

segments.en: This first one is a really great phrase because it's very, well, it's easy to picture this what we're describing.
segments.zh: 第一个是一个非常棒的短语，因为它非常非常好，很容易理解我们所描述的内容。

segments.en: This is a way to say that someone is sweating a lot.
segments.zh: 这是一种说某人出汗很多的方式。

segments.en: And it's really gross or disgusting.
I don't know if pigs actually sweat but you imagine someone smells bad and they have sweat on their face and their back and their arms.
segments.zh: 我不知道猪是否真的出汗，但你想象有人闻起来很臭，他们的脸上、背部和手臂上都有汗水。

segments.en: Well, sometimes don't you say you're sweating like a dog?
segments.zh: 好吧，有时你不是说你像狗一样出汗吗？

segments.en: I guess we like animals in English but this is just a really great way to say that someone is really sweaty.
segments.zh: 我想我们喜欢英语中的动物，但这只是说某人真的出汗的好方法。

segments.en: And well, he was sweating and he was really nervous because he said, I can't go through with this.
segments.zh: 好吧，他出汗了，他真的很紧张，因为他说，我无法忍受。

segments.en: What does he mean go through with this?
To go through with means to actually do something.
So maybe I say, I don't want to jump out of an airplane.
segments.zh: 所以也许我说，我不想跳下飞机。

segments.en: I can't go through with this.
So it depends on what we're actually talking about.
segments.zh: 所以这取决于我们实际在谈论什么。

segments.en: If we're talking about a wedding, you say, I can't go through with this.
segments.zh: 如果我们谈论的是婚礼，你说，我无法完成这个。

segments.en: So if you're planning a robbery, you say, well, in the last minute, I couldn't go through with it.
segments.zh: 所以如果你计划抢劫，你会说，在最后一分钟，我无法完成它。

segments.en: I can't complete what I talked about doing.
segments.zh: 我无法完成我所说的所做的事情。

segments.en: And now the friend, he finally gets kind of angry and he says, cut the crap.
segments.zh: 而现在的朋友，他终于有点生气了，他说，剪掉了废话。

segments.en: Oh man, this is a very common phrase.
segments.zh: 哦，伙计，这是一个非常常见的短语。

segments.en: This is someone says this if they don't want to listen to you complain anymore.
segments.zh: 如果他们不想再听你抱怨，这是有人这么说的。

segments.en: I don't want to hear your excuses.
I don't want to hear your complaints.
I want to just hear solutions, solutions, ideas, positive things.
segments.zh: 我只想听到解决方案、解决方案、想法、积极的事物。

segments.en: So to cut the crap is no more complaints, no more excuses or no more talking nonsense.
segments.zh: 因此，减少废话不再是抱怨，不再有借口或不再胡说八道。

segments.en: And this is, this is common among teachers and well, parents.
segments.zh: 这就是，这在老师和家长中很常见。

segments.en: Now it's not very polite, right?
So you wouldn't really say it to your boss or like a friend.
segments.zh: 所以你不会真的对你的老板或朋友说。

segments.en: Cut the crap is kind of rude and it's very spoken language.
segments.zh: Cut the Crap 有点粗鲁，而且是非常口头的语言。

segments.en: So I wouldn't write it down and I would not use this with someone who is like a teacher.
segments.zh: 所以我不会把它写下来，我也不会和像老师一样的人使用它。
好吧，就像一个权威一样。

segments.en: You don't use it with them.
segments.zh: 你不和他们一起使用它。

segments.en: They might use it with you.
segments.zh: 他们可能会和你一起使用它。

segments.en: And for our last phrase, he said, whew, you had me going there for a while or you had me going there for a minute.
segments.zh: 对于我们的最后一句话，他说，哇，你让我去那里一段时间，或者你让我去那里一分钟。

segments.en: So this is a really interesting phrase.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个非常有趣的短语。

segments.en: We use this a lot in English, but it's not clear from listening to it what it might mean.
segments.zh: 我们在英语中经常使用它，但听它不清楚它可能意味着什么。

segments.en: So you had me going there in this sense means, Oh, I was really nervous for a minute.
segments.zh: 所以你让我从这个意义上说，哦，我真的很紧张。

segments.en: I really believed what you were saying.
segments.zh: 我真的相信你在说什么。

segments.en: So maybe we could give an example, Marco.
segments.zh: 所以也许我们可以举一个例子，Marco。

segments.en: Um, did you know that yesterday I won the lottery?
segments.zh: 嗯，你知道昨天我中了彩票吗？

segments.en: I mean, I won like a million dollars and I had the perfect numbers.
segments.zh: 我的意思是，我赢了一百万美元，我有完美的数字。

segments.en: Can I have a million dollars?
segments.zh: 我可以有一百万美元吗？

segments.en: I would love to help you out, man.
But uh, yeah, no, I didn't actually win a million dollars.
segments.zh: 但是，嗯，是的，不，我实际上并没有赢得一百万美元。

segments.en: You had me going there for a minute.
segments.zh: 刚才有一阵我还真被你唬住了。

segments.en: You actually did for a little while.
segments.zh: 你实际上做了一段时间。
他不是那么容易上当受骗。

segments.en: But that, that's what it means, right?
segments.zh: 但这就是它的意思，对吧？

segments.en: To believe someone's story or to think that, um, something's going to happen even though it doesn't.
segments.zh: 相信某人的故事或这样想，嗯，即使没有，也会发生一些事情。

segments.en: That means what you thought was going to happen, didn't happen.
segments.zh: 这意味着你认为会发生的事情，没有发生。

segments.en: So you can use it in the third person, it's like, yeah, I was telling him this awesome story and I really had him going for a while.
segments.zh: 所以你可以在第三人称中使用它，就像，是的，我告诉他这个很棒的故事，我真的让他去了一段时间。

segments.en: And then I told him it wasn't true.
segments.zh: 然后我告诉他这不是真的。

segments.en: Now, let's listen to our dialogue for the last time and we'll be back to talk a little bit more about getting cold feet.
segments.zh: 现在，让我们最后一次听听我们的对话，我们会回来多谈谈谈到冷脚的事情。

I can't go through with this.
I've got my entire life ahead of me.
segments.zh: 我的一生都在等待着我。

segments.zh: 她不仅会被羞辱并杀死你，而且她是你爱的女人和你梦寐以求的女人。

segments.en: Why would you want to end that or jeopardize it like this?
segments.zh: 你为什么要结束它或像这样危及它？

segments.en: Second of all, you were just getting cold feet.
You know deep down inside that you'd want to marry her.
segments.zh: 你内心深处知道你会想嫁给她。

segments.en: So cut the crap and do it.
segments.zh: 所以别废话了，去结婚吧。

segments.en: You had me going there for a minute.
segments.zh: 刚才有一阵我还真被你唬住了。

segments.en: I thought I was going to have to slap some sense into you.
segments.zh: 我还以为得抽你几巴掌才能让你清醒呢。

segments.en: Alright, so this is a popular scenario, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，这是一个流行的场景，对吧？

segments.en: Everybody on their wedding day, they get cold feet and they back out.
segments.zh: 每个人在婚礼当天，他们都冷了下来，然后退缩了。

segments.en: TV, movies, books, everyone loves this situation.
segments.zh: 电视、电影、书籍，每个人都喜欢这种情况。

segments.en: Have you ever actually heard of or experienced or maybe known of somebody who actually left the bride at the altar or the groom at the altar?
segments.zh: 你有没有听说过、经历过或可能知道有人在祭坛上或在祭坛上的新郎上把新娘留在了新娘的地方？

segments.en: I don't know anyone who did that.
Luckily, I think it's really sad.
segments.zh: 幸运的是，我认为这真的很悲伤。

segments.en: I don't think it's really that common.
segments.zh: 我不认为这真的很常见。

segments.en: No, but there was a movie just about this.
segments.zh: 不，但有一部电影就是关于这个的。

segments.en: So there's a woman, Julia Roberts, who tries and tries and tries to get married but never can so it's called Runaway Bride because every time she goes to the altar, she gets nervous.
segments.zh: 所以有一个女人，朱莉娅·罗伯茨，她试图结婚，但永远不能结婚，所以这被称为失控的新娘，因为每次她去祭坛时，她都会变得紧张。

segments.en: She gets cold feet and she runs away.
They call her the Runaway Bride.
segments.zh: 他们称她为逃跑的新娘。

segments.en: I can't imagine this actually happening to someone.
segments.zh: 我无法想象这实际上发生在某人身上。

segments.en: I mean, you have all your family there, your friends.
segments.zh: 我的意思是，你所有的家人，你的朋友都在那里。

segments.en: Exactly, because you've already paid for everything.
segments.zh: 没错，因为你已经付出了一切。

segments.en: So do you get to eat the cake if you're the one who's left behind?
segments.zh: 那么，如果你是被抛在后面的那一位，你可以吃蛋糕吗？

segments.en: Alright, so that's all the time we have for today.
segments.zh: 好吧，这就是我们今天所拥有的所有时间。
